candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall ensure that the sewage sludge meets the requirements in 40 CFR 258 concerning the quality of the sludge dispose d in a municipal solid waste landfill unit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Incorporation of 40 CFR 258 by reference can supply enforceable pollutant/quality criteria (Purpose A) and associated monitoring or testing obligations (Purpose B); how broadly 'requirements ... concerning the quality of the sludge' is read changes which limits and monitoring apply.

candidates.exact_span: Sewage sludge shall be tested once during the life of the permit within one year from the effective date of the permit in accordance with the method specified at 40 CFR 268, Appendix I (Toxicity Characteristic Leaching Procedure (TCLP)) or other approved methods.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether TCLP monitoring was required during Federal FY2025 depends on permit effective date, whether the one-time/within-one-year window has passed, and whether an 'other approved method' satisfies the obligation; missing or ambiguous timing changes required-vs-not-required and missing-evidence classification.

candidates.exact_span: Sludge shall be tested after final treatment prior to leaving the POTW site.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The sampling point and timing condition define when the TCLP obligation must be met; different readings of 'final treatment' or 'prior to leaving the POTW site' change whether reported samples satisfy the monitoring requirement.

candidates.exact_span: Sewage sludge determined to be a hazardous waste in accordance with 40 CFR Part 261, shall be handled according to RCRA standards for the disposal of hazardous waste in accordance with 40 CFR Part 262.
candidates.computation_change_reason: A hazardous-waste classification shifts compliance from ordinary numeric sludge-quality limits to RCRA handling/disposal rules (Purpose A) and changes what documented outcomes or missing data mean when TCLP/261 criteria are implicated (Purpose C).

candidates.exact_span: The disposal of sewage sludge determined to be a hazardous waste, in other than a certified hazardous waste disposal facility shall be prohibited.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This prohibition functions as an enforceable compliance standard for sludge classified as hazardous waste; interpreting whether sludge is 'determined to be a hazardous waste' changes whether this limit applies instead of or in addition to numeric quality limits.

candidates.exact_span: A written report shall be provided to this office within 7 days after failing the TCLP.
candidates.computation_change_reason: A failed TCLP triggers a distinct documented reporting state; absence of both numeric results and this report must be distinguished from no-discharge, not-required monitoring, or unresolved missing evidence.

candidates.exact_span: Sewage sludge shall be tested as needed, or at a minimum, once/year in accordance with the method 9095 (Paint Filter Liquids Test) as described in "Test Methods for Evaluating Solid Wastes, Physical/Chemical Methods" (EPA Pub. No. SW-846).
candidates.computation_change_reason: The 'as needed' qualifier versus the 'at a minimum, once/year' floor governs annual Paint Filter monitoring frequency in FY2025 (Purpose B); when conditional monitoring is not triggered, periods without results may be not-required rather than missing required evidence (Purpose C).
